observations:
Torah #268 contains no explicit bechina language anywhere in its three paragraphs. The requirement for a new package proposal is: 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. This condition is not met.

The teaching operates through pure eitza logic — every relationship in the text is causal and sequential:
- The soul withdraws BECAUSE the person does not do God's will (eitza)
- The person gets sick BECAUSE the soul weakens (eitza)
- The soul returns BECAUSE it sees the person can subdue his desire (eitza)
- The person recovers BECAUSE the soul returns (eitza)

The key concepts of the Torah — נֶפֶשׁ (soul), תַּכְלִית (purpose), תַּאֲוָה (desire), רְפוּאוֹת (medicine/healing), בְּרִיאוּת (health) — do not appear in any 'X הוא בחינת Y' construction in this text. They are not being identified as parallel aspects of a shared essence; they are actors and states in a moral-psychological argument.

The Torah's single insight is structural-eitza: the soul's mechanism for withdrawing from a spiritually negligent body is the same mechanism invoked when the body heals through medicine (demonstrating capacity to subdue desire). This parallel is an eitza analogy ('just as the person subdues desire for health, so should he for God'), not a bechina equivalence ('medicine IS an aspect of God's will').

Conclusion: No new packages can be proposed. This Torah is correctly represented in the dataset as having zero bechina edges. A complete representation of Torah #268 would consist entirely of eitza edges connecting: אי-הסתכלות על התכלית → נסיגת הנפש → חולי; and כפיית התאוה → חזרת הנפש → בריאות; with the teaching's climax being the eitza from כפיית התאוה לתכלית האמתי toward the ultimate goal of עשיית רצון יוצרו.
